rows.note: This is the colloquial all-purpose choice for laughing at or making fun of someone contemptuously.

example.english: They always scoff at other people's accents.
example.jyutping: keoi5 seng4 jat6 siu3 jan4 dei6 ge3 hau2 jam1

rows.note: Use this when explicitly describing derisive mockery rather than ordinary joking or teasing.

example.english: They all scoff at his failure.
example.traditional: 全班同學都嘲笑佢嘅失敗。
example.jyutping: cyun4 baan1 tung4 hok6 dou1 zaau1 siu3 keoi5 ge3 sat1 baai6

rows.note: Use this when the mockery clearly expresses contempt or is intended to humiliate the target.

example.english: Don't scoff at people in public; it really hurts.
example.traditional: 你唔好當眾恥笑人，咁樣好傷人㗎。
example.jyutping: nei5 m4 hou2 dong1 zung3 ci2 siu3 jan4 gam3 joeng2 hou2 soeng1 jan4 gaa3
